mapName: A Learnable Meta Latin America - Intermediate

metas.name: Argentina - Chevrons
metas.note:
Argentina typically uses white-and-red chevrons.

NOTE: Argentina is the only country in the Americas with these chevrons.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Brazil - Bahia and Pernambuco pole markings
metas.note: Markings on poles are used by the electricity companies to identify them. This pole ID is long, yellow pole paint with a black code. The ones that start with a letter are found in Bahia and Pernambuco.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Carnauba Palms
metas.note: Carnaúba palms have short but strong fan-like leaves, and a trunk that is smooth at the top and spiked at the bottom. They are commonly seen in Ceará, Piauí, and Rio Grande de Norte, but are also around the town of Xique Xique in Bahia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Ceará lamps
metas.note: Lamps in Ceará often have a fancy and colourful arm, whether as lampposts or attached to utility poles. It sometimes says the town on the arm.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Ceara pole top
metas.note: This asymmetrical concrete crossbar with no supports is exclusive to Ceara.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Coffee beans
metas.note: Coffee beans are by far the most common in Minas Gerais, but also can be found in Espírito Santo and northeastern São Paulo.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Concrete bins
metas.note: Brazil often uses metal trash baskets outside houses. In Acre and Rondônia, however, it is much more common to see them made of concrete.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Espírito Santo - Exposed rock
metas.note: Espírito Santo, and the surrounding areas, often have large mountains with exposed rock.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Goiás pole markings
metas.note: Similar to the Bahia and Pernambuco poles, Goiás poles also use long, yellow pole paint with a black paint code, but it always starts with a number. They also have a rarer yellow on black pole ID, which can be either paint or a plate.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Maranhão wide insulators
metas.note: Poles with these wide insulators in a trident formation are common in Maranhão. The insulator itself is common across many states, but not in this configuration.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Mato Grosso pole
metas.note: Poles that have one insulator on top and alternating horizontal insulators can be found in Mato Grosso and southern Acre. It is also very rare in Rio Grande do Sul.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Paraná pines
metas.note: These distinct trees, called Paraná pines, have long horizontal branches with leaves only at the end. They grow mainly in the southern Brazilian states of Paraná, Santa Catarina, and Rio Grande do Sul.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Piauí road
metas.note:
Many roads in Piauí have red gravel on the side of the road. The gravel can appear spread above the tarmac shoulder or on roads with curbs.

NOTE: This can appear elsewhere. Use with caution.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Rolling grassy hills
metas.note: Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo often have rolling grassy hills.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Rural Roraima
metas.note: Rural locations in Roraima are mostly open grassy plains with large, distant mountains in the background. Occasionally, you are on roads within the mountains. Furthermore, the grass in Roraima is distinctly thin, and grows in bunches.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Sugarcane plantations
metas.note: Sugarcane plantations are by far most common in the state of São Paulo, and are common in Paraná, Mato Grosso do Sul, and in the coastal north eastern states.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Very tall grass
metas.note: Very tall grass can be often seen in the centre of the country, most notably in the Tocantins, Goiás, Bahia, and Minas Gerais states.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Colombia - Antioquia pole paint
metas.note: These pole markings with one short black strip on the top and bottom, and a longer yellow section in the middle, are most commonly found in the Antioquia department. Sometimes, you can find them in the Cordoba department as well.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/colombia for more clues.

metas.name: Ecuador - Ecuador shitcam
metas.note:
If you have vibes that you are in South America and coverage was taken using "shitcam" camera you gonna be in Ecuador. There is "shitcam" in other countries but in South America you can only find "shitcam" in Ecuador.

Note: Ecuador also has GEN3(and little bit of GEN4) coverage not only shitcam! So don't discard Ecuador if it's not shitcam.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Agave salmiana
metas.note: Agave salmiana, also known as pulque agaves, have wide, smooth, curling leaves, and a crown-like appearance. They are common in the central Mexican valley and further north around the city of San Luis Potosi.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Agave tequilana
metas.note: Vast fields of blue agave (Agave tequilana), used to produce tequila, are mostly found in Jalisco and Nayarit.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Blindingly white soil
metas.note:
Almost blindingly white soil in the Yucatan peninsula is most common in Quintana Roo.

NOTE: This is only consistent in Generation 3.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Blue Myrtle Cacti
metas.note: The Blue Myrtle Cacti have short arms that uniformly curve and point upwards. It is abundantly found in San Luis Potosi, but also common in Queretaro and Hidalgo.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Boojum trees
metas.note: Boojum trees can be recognized by their alien, tentacle-like appearance. They are almost exclusively found in the southern half of Baja California.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Brittlebush
metas.note: Brittlebush are small shrubs with bright silver-grey leaves that are most commonly found in Sonora, especially around Hermosillo.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Chihuahua cross
metas.note: A thick cross can be seen on the back of signs in Chihuahua.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Cobblestone pavement
metas.note: This style of cobblestone pavement, unorganised with irregular tiles, can be found in most of the central states, but is by far most commonly found in the states of Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima, and Queretaro.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Concrete hanging insulator pole
metas.note: These concrete poles with insulators suspended below the crossbars are unique to the Yucatan peninsula.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Guanajuato extremely dark fields
metas.note: Extremely dark fields are common in Guanajuato.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Hexagonal tiles pavement
metas.note: This pavement consisting of hexagonal tiles is found in Puebla and Tlaxcala.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Light coloured rock walls
metas.note:
These walls made of light coloured rock are found in the Yucatan peninsula, but most common in Yucatan state.

Comment from Vincent: When not in the sun, the rock walls appear darker, but it's likely the same type of rock.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Nayarit bollard
metas.note: Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit, apart from one exception being Federal Highway 190 on the Oaxaca-Chiapas border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Oaxaca pavement
metas.note: This exact pavement design with three lines of cobblestone patterning is exclusive to Oaxaca.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Oil palm plantations
metas.note: Oil palm plantations are most common in Chiapas, and occasionally on the outskirts of the state in Veracruz, Tabasco, and Campeche.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Red agricultural fields
metas.note: Red agricultural fields are commonly seen in Zacatecas and occasionally southern Durango.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Rounded electric counter
metas.note:
Mexico uses those circular electricity counters.

You can find those in other countries:

  • Philippines(vegetation,climate will be different)
  • USA(looks different,English instead of Spanish etc)
  • Guatamela(has car meta)
  • Dominican Republic(has car meta)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Saguaro Cacti
metas.note: The Saguaro Cacti can be spotted in the western half of Sonora, featuring short curving arms that stem from a main trunk.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Wooden hanging insulator pole
metas.note: The wooden variant of the hanging pole is found on the Baja California peninsula.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Peru - Electricity counter
metas.note: Peru's electricity meters are rectangular and have horizontal rectangular openings. They look kinda like post boxes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.
